t: Subsection (b) of section 116 of the National Security Act of 1947 (50 U.S.C. 404k) is amended by striking the period at the end and inserting “, who may delegate such authority to other appropriate officials of the Central Intelligence Agency.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that delegating authority to 'other appropriate officials' brings additional parties into a decision. Those officials are all CIA employees, so the delegation stays entirely inside the federal government. The amendment creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside entities, rulemaking, or right to sue.
fable.s: who may delegate such authority to other appropriate officials of the Central Intelligence Agency

opus.w: This amendment only lets a federal official hand authority to other officials within the CIA. Everyone involved is inside the federal government, so this is not participation. The section has no comment period, hearing, advisory body with outside members, consultation with outsiders, or right to sue.
opus.s: who may delegate such authority to other appropriate officials of the Central Intelligence Agency.
opus.b: **Step 1: Tempting reading and why it fails.** Someone might see "delegate such authority to other appropriate officials" as a procedural step. But delegation happens entirely inside the federal government: the authority passes to "officials of the Central Intelligence Agency." No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public takes part in any federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section amends a statute to allow the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency to delegate authority to other officials within the agency. This is an internal administrative delegation between federal officials. It does not involve consultation, coordination, or participation with any party outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, the public, or private entities). Therefore, it does not meet the definition of participation.
qwen_chat.s: who may delegate such authority to other appropriate officials of the Central Intelligence Agency.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "other appropriate officials" could include non-federal contractors or advisors, thus implying participation. However, the context of the National Security Act and the Central Intelligence Agency strongly implies that "officials" refers to federal employees or appointees within the agency. Furthermore, the text describes an internal delegation of authority within the CIA, not a process for consulting with outsiders before making a decision.
